newsitem.title: UK: IPE oil futures spike up on stocks, short-covering.
newsitem.headline: IPE oil futures spike up on stocks, short-covering.

text.p: IPE Brent crude and product futures spiked higher following a report that stocks in the European Union fell in June and a stronger NYMEX opening saw Brent extending gains through $18.40 resistance, traders said.
"The market bounced up from support then through early resistance around $18.30 and subsequently triggered short-covering which pushed the market higher," one broker said.
By 1420 GMT the July Brent contract was trading one cent down at $18.37 a barrel after a sharp rise from around $18.24 took it briefly through resistance at $18.40 a barrel.
July gas oil was $1.50 firmer at $164.25 a tonne.
Traders said the next trendline resistance target was around $18.51 and this was likely to be achieved now the band of resistance up to $18.40 had been broken down.
Gas oil was hitting resistance at around $164-$164.25 analysts said this corresponds to a gap on the front month continuation chart from last Thursday to Friday.
Crude and oil product stocks in the 15 countries of the European Union plus Norway all fell in June, Stitching Euroilstock said in its latest monthly report.
They said crude stocks fell the most, dropping 11.61 million barrels, or 2.7 percent, in June to 416.90 million barrels, leaving them 8.91 million barrels, or 2.1 percent, lower than year-ago.

Middle distillate stocks fell by 1.65 million barrels, or 0.5 percent, to 314.40 million barrels. This left them 15.15 million barrels, or 5.1 percent, higher than a year ago. --Colin Wooster, London Newsroom, +44 171 542 7456
